comment: Single source of truth for the EN screencast narration. Emotion tags ([excited], [pause], ...) are ElevenLabs v3 audio tags and are stripped for subtitles. Voice/model live here (not secrets); ELEVENLABS_VOICE_ID_EN / ELEVENLABS_MODEL_ID env vars override. First-class English copy translated from narration-manifest-de.json; same 39 markers, identical emotion tags. Segments 21-24, 26, 28 follow the button-driven kanban workflow (ADR-009) — no drag-and-drop.

segments.description: Welcome to the BATbern event management platform
segments.text: [excited] Welcome to the BATbern event management platform! [playful] Today I'll show you how to plan an event without losing your mind. [chuckling] We'll walk through the complete event lifecycle, from "Oh no, we need an event" all the way to "Finally over, straight into the archive with it!" [pause] In this video you'll see all the key steps an organizer takes to plan a Berner Architekten Treffen, without breaking into a panic.

[cheerful] We start at the event dashboard. [playful] Think of it as your command center, where you keep an overview of every event you've ever organized or ever will. [pause] Authentication via AWS Cognito is already taken care of. [satisfied] You can see your username in the top right corner, and with it you have the power to use every organizer feature. [dramatic] With great power comes great responsibility!

[cheerful] By the way, the platform speaks many languages! [playful] Top right, in the user menu, you'll find the language selector. [excited] A full ten languages are available — from German, English, French and Italian all the way to Romansh and even Bernese German! [satisfied] For this video, let's switch the whole platform to English.

[enthusiastic] Now let's create a brand new event! [excited] Click the "New Event" button in the top right. [pause] Boom! A modal form appears. [playful] Don't worry, it looks like a lot, but we'll fill it out together.

[professional] Event number. [casual] A unique identifier for this event. Internally the system uses the format "BATbern" followed by the number. [playful] Think of it as your event's birth certificate. It's used for identification in the database and in URLs.

[short pause] Title. [cheerful] This is the name that's supposed to wow your attendees! [playful] "Boring Architecture Event Number 47" would be honest, but maybe not the best choice. [chuckling] Pick something compelling that people will see on the public website.

[short pause] Description. [casual] A brief explanation of the event topic. [helpful] This information helps prospects understand why they absolutely must sign up. [playful] Or at least what it's all about.

[pause] Event type. [professional] Choose between three formats: [clear] "Evening" for after-work events, [cheerful] where you can do a bit of networking once the workday is done. "Afternoon" for afternoon events, [playful] perfect for anyone who'd rather be on the couch in the evening. [pause] Or "Full day" for all-day conferences. [dramatic] You'll need a lot of coffee for those! [short pause] This affects scheduling and slot management.

[professional] Date and registration deadline. [clear] The event date sets when the event takes place. [playful] Please pick a date in the future, we don't support time travel just yet. [chuckling] The registration deadline is important for managing attendees.

[short pause] Venue. [casual] The name and address of the venue. [playful] So not "in my basement", but a real place with an actual address. [cheerful] This information is shown on the public website, so people can actually find their way there.

[satisfied] We click "Save" and the event is created. [excited] Ta-da! [pause] The system automatically returns to the dashboard, and there it is! Your brand new event in the list. [playful] Your baby is born!

segments.description: Navigate to the event detail page
segments.text: [pause] After creating the event, we navigate to the event detail page. [professional] Here we can assign tasks to team members. [playful] Because why would you do everything yourself when you have a whole team? [chuckling] Click "Edit" to reopen the event form.

[clear] Switch to the "Tasks" tab. [professional] Here you'll see a predefined list of standard tasks that come up for every event. [playful] The system knows its stuff, it knows everything that needs doing. [pause] For each task we pick a responsible organizer from the dropdown menu. [helpful] This makes sure every important activity is clearly assigned and nothing gets forgotten. [dramatic] Because forgotten tasks lead to chaos, and chaos leads to... well, more chaos.
[confident] After assigning, we click "Save". [satisfied] The system saves all the tasks and returns to the event detail page. [cheerful] Perfect!

[pause] To review the tasks, we navigate to the task list. [informative] At first you see the default "My Tasks" filter, which shows only your own tasks. [playful] But we're curious and want to know what everyone else is up to. [chuckling] We switch the filter to "All Tasks" to see every assignment. This gives an overview of responsibilities across the whole team. [whispers] And who might just have nothing to do right now.
[excited] Back on the event detail page, we begin the content planning! [enthusiastic] The first step is topic selection. Click "Select Topic".
[cheerful] A view opens with various topic categories. The default view shows a list, [excited] but we'll use the heat map for a better overview. [playful] Because who doesn't love a good heat map?

[curious] The heat map is a two-dimensional matrix that visualizes topics by their popularity and timeliness. [excited] Bright colors show popular topics, [casual] basically the rock stars among architecture topics. [pause] Darker colors show less frequently chosen topics. [playful] The underdogs, who deserve a chance too. [helpful] This helps with strategic topic planning based on the interests of the attendees.

[instructional] We pick a topic from the heat map by clicking a cell. [satisfied] The system marks the selection and shows details. [excited] After confirming, the system saves the chosen topic and automatically opens the speaker brainstorming view. [playful] The system is like a good assistant, it always knows what comes next!

[enthusiastic] Now we gather potential speakers for the chosen topic! [professional] In this phase we build a pool of candidates we'll contact later. [pause] We add five speaker candidates. [strategic] This gives us plenty of options for reaching out, in case not everyone says yes. [playful] Because speakers are like cats, sometimes they just say no, for no reason at all.

[confident] After adding all the candidates, we click "Continue to Contacting". [satisfied] The system automatically switches to the kanban view, where we can track contact status. [excited] Kanban! That sounds important and organized!

[professional] We're now in the speaker contacting phase. [informative] The kanban board shows the workflow in columns — from "Identified" through "Contacted" and "Ready" to "Accepted". [playful] From "Who's that?" to "Hooray, they said yes!" [helpful] And the best part: every card has an action button that always offers you exactly the next sensible step. [satisfied] No more guessing what to do next.

[methodical] Now we systematically contact all five speaker candidates. [instructional] For each candidate we click "Log Contact" on the card. [professional] In the dialog we choose the contact method, for example email or phone, and capture notes about the response. [playful] Otherwise next week someone asks: "Did we already contact this person?" And nobody knows. [chuckling] Chaos avoided! [satisfied] The cards automatically move into the "Contacted" column.

[positive] Three candidates responded positively. [excited] Time to promote them to actual speakers! [instructional] A click on "Promote to Speaker" opens the detail view. There we create a user account for Nissim, Baltisar and Andreas, each with a name and an email address. [informative] This gives them access to the speaker portal later. [playful] The system handles all the paperwork in the background. [satisfied] The three cards move into the "Ready" column.

[confident] Now we record the acceptances. [informative] Normally speakers receive an invitation and respond themselves in the speaker portal. [casual] But if they've already agreed verbally, we record that directly. [instructional] We open Nissim's card, choose "Record Acceptance on Behalf" and give a short reason. [satisfied] Nissim is on board!

[cheerful] On to Baltisar from Galenica. [instructional] We open his card too, again choose "Record Acceptance on Behalf" and confirm with a short note. [playful] Two out of three — running like clockwork!

[enthusiastic] And Andreas from Mobiliar? [satisfied] On board as well! [instructional] We record his acceptance on his behalf too, again with a short reason. [excited] That gives us three confirmed speakers — enough to fill the evening.

segments.description: Daniel declines + Vanessa stays in pool
segments.text: [playful] And Daniel? [dramatic] Daniel unfortunately doesn't have time. [casual] We decline him with "Decline with Reason" — with a reason too, of course. [informative] We deliberately leave Vanessa in the pool as a candidate, in case we end up needing someone later after all. [chuckling] Speakers really are like cats.

[important] Before speakers can submit their content, we need to publish the topic. [instructional] We navigate to the "Publishing" tab and click "Publish Topic". [informative] At the bottom you can see a preview of the event on the public page. [satisfied] Nice, isn't it?

[professional] Back in the kanban, we now capture the presentation content for each confirmed speaker. [instructional] The action button is now called "Add Content". [casual] Title, abstract, the usual suspects. The speaker is already linked automatically. [methodical] We repeat this process for all three speakers. [playful] Copy, paste, repeat. [chuckling] No, just kidding, every speaker has unique content, of course!

[professional] The content is submitted. [instructional] Next we make the speakers public: we click "Publish Speakers". [excited] And here it comes! [satisfied] Now the public website shows not just the topic, but also the confirmed speakers with their talks. [cheerful] The whole world can see it!

[pause] And now comes the actual quality review. [professional] Back in the kanban, we review each submitted presentation. [instructional] This time the action button is called "Review Content". [playful] Now we're playing quality control. [pause] Looks good, looks good, that one too. [confident] We approve all three presentations. [satisfied] Green light for everyone!
[instructional] For slot assignment we switch to the sessions view. Click "Manage Slot Assignments". [pause] Now it's about timing!

[enthusiastic] For a quick initial plan we use the auto-assign function. [excited] The system performs the automatic assignment. [playful] Magic! The system does the work. [informative] Manual assignment via drag-and-drop is also possible here. [casual] In case you don't trust the computer, or just enjoy moving things around.
[calm] After the slot assignment, we click "Back to Event".

[dramatic] The final step is publishing the agenda! [enthusiastic] The grand finale! [instructional] Click "Publish Agenda". [triumphant] And... [excited] The event is now fully planned and publicly accessible, including a detailed agenda! [cheerful] Confetti! Fireworks! Okay, maybe just in our heads, but still! [satisfied] We made it!

[excited] And there's our event — live on the public website! [satisfied] Let's slowly scroll through the page. [cheerful] At the very top the title with date and location, below it the speakers with their talks, and finally the complete agenda with every time slot. [playful] This is exactly what your attendees see when they register. [satisfied] Looks fantastic, doesn't it?
[pause] After running the event, we archive it for the records. [professional] Switch to the "Overview" tab and click "Edit". [playful] Time to send the event into retirement.
[clear] In the form, select "ARCHIVED" as the status. [casual] The event was great, but now it's history.

[informative] For testing purposes you can override the workflow validation. [instructional] Tick the "Override Workflow Validation" checkbox and click "Save". [playful] Think of it as the emergency exit, for when things don't quite go to plan.

[triumphant] And that completes the full event workflow! [excited] From the first idea to the archive, we made the whole journey together! [satisfied] You're now an event management pro! [cheerful] Thank you so much for your attention! [playful] And remember: planning events is fun, [chuckling] at least with the right software! [laughing] Bye!
